channel.title: MAXGEN — the open genealogy standard, explained
channel.description: Eight conversations explaining MAXGEN, the open probabilistic genealogy data standard: one overview and one episode per schema.
channel.itunes:author: OpenGenealogyAI

item.title: The MAXGEN Overview
item.description: Why genealogy data needs a common language, the seven schemas, and the design philosophy behind them.

item.title: MaxRecord — Source documents as written
item.description: Evidence versus interpretation, and why the clerk who wrote 'Makeswell' must never be corrected.

item.title: MaxPerson — The person who might be your ancestor
item.description: Assertions not facts, probabilistic parents, composite confidence, and the merge model.

item.title: MaxTask — Distributing the work
item.description: Task types, the verdict vocabulary, acceptance criteria, and the anti-hallucination rule.

item.title: MaxDNA — Genetic evidence without giving up privacy
item.description: Hashed kit IDs, consent, endogamy, phasing, and how DNA boosts documentary confidence.

item.title: MaxSource — The routing brain
item.description: Where records hide: coverage, access, provenance, and semantic search over sources.

item.title: MaxRecognition — Teaching machines to read
item.description: OCR and handwriting provenance, word-level confidence, labelled inference, and consensus.

item.title: MaxName — Why Maxwell and Makeswell are the same family
item.description: Variants, cognates, phonetic keys, and the council design process behind the newest schema.
